assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection changed how trade is modelled. It explains who exports, why gains from trade operate through reallocation across firms, and how trade liberalisation affects aggregate productivity. The framework is now the workhorse of international trade and is used widely in empirical work on firm-level data.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central theoretical contribution. Helpman has a long record of building the broader theory, including the multi-country and trade-and-labour-market extensions with Melitz and Yeaple. Redding is an important later contributor, particularly on quantitative and spatial extensions, but is more clearly a successor to the core idea. A two-person prize is the cleanest attribution.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation. The results are well replicated, are taught in graduate trade courses, and underpin the quantitative trade literature. The field has not been recognised since Krugman in 2008.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to pair Melitz with Eaton-Kortum-style quantitative work on the gains from trade, or to include Redding.
My assessment relies on general knowledge and the longlist description, not on independent verification of the literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework are the foundation of modern monetary policy analysis in central banks. Staggered contracts, the Calvo pricing mechanism, interest-rate rules and the microfounded model of policy are all central to this body of work.
assessment.attribution: Taylor contributed staggered wage contracts and the policy rule. Calvo contributed the tractable time-dependent pricing model. Woodford systematised the framework and its normative analysis. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets made major contributions on estimation and empirical models. The three-name limit forces hard exclusions.
assessment.maturity: Very mature. The framework has been used in policy for decades. Bernanke's 2022 prize touched monetary policy only indirectly, via the banking and Great Depression work, so the core New Keynesian contributions remain unrecognised.
uncertainties: Credit is spread across many contributors, and the three-name limit makes the exclusions contestable.
Debate persists over how well the framework performed in the post-2020 inflation episode.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) showed how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks into credit cycles. This is a foundational mechanism for understanding financial crises and for modern macro-finance models.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki-Moore is a tightly defined paper-level contribution with clear authorship. Gertler and Gilchrist are important for the financial accelerator and its empirical evidence, but they sit alongside rather than inside the central mechanism. Bernanke already holds a prize for the related work on banking and the Great Depression.
assessment.maturity: Well established. The mechanism is widely used in macro and policy models and has been confirmed in studies of the 2008 crisis.
uncertainties: The 2022 prize partially covered the financial-crisis theme, which may reduce the field's priority.
Whether the committee prefers the Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist accelerator strand or the Kiyotaki-Moore strand.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bridging optimal-tax theory and empirical evidence on behavioural responses, through the elasticity of taxable income and sufficient-statistics methods, has reshaped tax policy analysis and the discussion of top rates. The work directly informs policy design.
assessment.attribution: Saez is central both for the theory-to-evidence linkage and for the top-income applications. Slemrod made earlier major contributions on the behavioural response to taxation and on tax avoidance. Chetty and Stantcheva are important, but Chetty's credit is spread across several strands and Stantcheva's work is more recent.
assessment.maturity: Substantially mature for Saez and Slemrod. Debates about elasticity magnitudes and identification continue.
uncertainties: Overlap with the inequality candidate B020 in Saez's work could split support.
The elasticity of taxable income remains contested, since estimates are sensitive to design and to the type of income.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based framework for technology and labour demand, and the China-shock evidence on local labour-market adjustment, have changed how economists and policymakers understand inequality, polarisation and the distributional costs of trade. Both strands draw on credible empirical design and have strong policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Autor is common to both strands. Hanson is central to the trade-shock work with Autor and Dorn. Katz and Acemoglu (already a laureate) are important for the skill-biased technical change tradition. Dorn is a co-author on the trade-shock work. The two-name proposal reflects the separation between the technology and trade contributions.
assessment.maturity: Mature enough. The key papers date from roughly 2003 to 2016 and have been widely replicated and debated.
uncertainties: Some reassessment of the China-shock magnitudes and of the task framework's empirical content is ongoing.
Credit overlaps with a prize already awarded for technology and institutions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Persson, Tabellini and Besley built the modern theory and empirics of political economics, linking constitutions, electoral rules, state capacity and fiscal outcomes. The work is a rigorous, systematic synthesis with a broad empirical programme.
assessment.attribution: The attribution is clear and well matched, since the three authors worked jointly and separately on the core agenda. Their individual papers and books are well known as a coherent programme.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The work spans three decades, and the field has produced a large empirical literature building on it.
uncertainties: The 2024 prize to Acemoglu, Johnson and Robinson recognised adjacent institutions research, which may reduce the priority of this area.
Causal identification in the constitutional-effects work is harder than in the more design-based fields.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data have transformed the measurement of intergenerational mobility and of neighbourhood and school effects. The work changed the empirical agenda and policy debate. The use of register data is close to the Swedish and Nordic empirical tradition, but I assess it by common criteria.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear leader of the programme, and Hendren, Friedman and Katz are key collaborators. Because the programme is collaborative and recent, a single-name proposal is the most defensible, though it carries risk of contested credit.
assessment.maturity: Less mature than the higher-ranked candidates. The main findings date from about 2014 onward, and the causal neighbourhood-effects results are still being replicated and refined.
uncertainties: Credit among collaborators is contested, and a single-name prize would slight them.
The methodological novelty is largely in data access and scale rather than in new identification strategies.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Social preferences, meaning reciprocity, fairness and inequity aversion, brought a disciplined, testable alternative to purely selfish preferences. The experimental evidence on ultimatum, public-goods and gift-exchange games, together with the Fehr-Schmidt model, has influenced theory across fields.
assessment.attribution: Fehr is the central empirical and conceptual figure. Schmidt contributed the inequity-aversion model with Fehr that reconciled the experimental evidence. Falk is an important later contributor. Rabin's earlier fairness work is not on the credited list, so the credit boundary is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The results are about 25 years old and have been replicated widely, though debates continue about external validity.
uncertainties: Behavioural economics was recognised with Kahneman (2002) and Thaler (2017), so the committee may regard the area as already covered.
Generalisability of lab results to field settings remains debated.
